region: Watkins Glen · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Lakewood Vineyards is a three-generation family winery on the west shore of Seneca Lake, just north of Watkins Glen. The Stamps settled at Lakewood Farm in 1951 and grew grapes for juice processors and big wineries for decades, before planting fine wine varieties in the 1980s and opening their winery in 1989. Today Chris Stamp makes the wine and his brother Dave manages about 100 acres of certified-sustainable vineyards. Their range runs from dry Riesling to this fortified red for the end of the meal.

Lakewood’s Port is made in the Portuguese manner, fortified to around 18% alcohol, but from the cold-hardy hybrid grapes that thrive in the Finger Lakes rather than Douro varieties. The winery describes it as made from very ripe, partly raisined Baco Noir; other vintages have included Frontenac and Vincent. Leaving the grapes to shrivel concentrates their sugar and flavour. Lakewood describes a deep scarlet wine with black raspberry and currant on the nose and a velvety, warm palate with cassis and a hint of anise.
facts: Primarily Baco Noir (other vintages also Frontenac, Vincent)
